posts.headline: A women's seed bank now supports *5,000+ farmers, 30 villages*
posts.body: The Bibi Fatima Women's Self-Help Group of Teertha village, Dharwad (Karnataka), protects indigenous seeds and millets. On 12 Nov, it won the national Plant Genome Saviour Community Award and ₹10 lakh.
posts.source: The Better India (23 Nov 2026), Drishti IAS (17 Nov 2026), Adda247 (14 Nov 2026), UNDP (8 Aug 2025), Down To Earth (13 Aug 2025)
posts.caption:
Their seed bank feeds 5,000+ farmers 🌾

In Teertha village in Karnataka's Dharwad district, the women of the Bibi Fatima Women's Self-Help Group, led by Bibijan Halemani, protect indigenous seeds and millets. Their work now supports more than 5,000 farmers across 30 villages, with solar-powered millet processing.

On 12 November in New Delhi, the group received the Plant Genome Saviour Community Award from the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Authority, with ₹10 lakh. In 2025, they were also one of 10 global winners of the UNDP Equator Prize. 🏆

Which traditional grain from your grandmother's kitchen would you love to see return? 👇

Sources: The Better India, UNDP, Down To Earth, Drishti IAS
Representative photo, not of the people named.

posts.headline: Tribal kitchens, *now in Mumbai*
posts.sub: Tata Steel Foundation's Samvaad brings tribal cuisine to The Great Indian Feast Trail, Mumbai, 27–29 Nov.

slides.title: Tribal recipes at *a 400+ dish festival*
slides.body: Samvaad joins The Great Indian Feast Trail at Jio World Garden, BKC: 13 regional food trails and 400+ dishes.

slides.title: One gathering, *353 tribal communities*
slides.body: Samvaad's 13th edition, held in Jamshedpur from 15 to 19 November, brought together 2,500+ participants.

slides.title: More than half were new
slides.body: And 15% came from Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).

posts.takeaway: Food is memory. When it's shared, *culture grows.*
posts.source: India CSR (27 Nov 2026), The Great Indian Feast Trail (official site), The Week (15 Nov 2026), ThePrint/PTI (14 Nov 2026)
posts.caption:
Mumbai, this weekend's menu is centuries old 🍃🔥

Tata Steel Foundation's Samvaad, its tribal culture programme, is bringing tribal cuisine to The Great Indian Feast Trail at Jio World Garden, BKC, from 27 to 29 November. The festival has 13 regional food trails and 400+ dishes.

Samvaad's 13th edition in Jamshedpur (15–19 November) brought together 2,500+ participants from 353 tribal communities. 55% were there for the first time, and 15% came from Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups. 💛

Food is memory and identity. Go taste it, and say hello.

Save this 🔖 and tag a friend in Mumbai who should try it.

Sources: India CSR, The Week, ThePrint (PTI), The Great Indian Feast Trail
Representative photos.

posts.headline: India's cheetahs: *nearly 70% born at home*
points: 9 cubs born at Kuno in two litters (5 Oct, 20 Nov)
Now living across 3 sites in Madhya Pradesh
posts.source: PIB via DD India (26 Nov 2026), The Week (20 Nov 2026), Business News Week (26 Nov 2026)
posts.caption:
India's cheetah family keeps growing 🐆💛

🐾 62 cheetahs now live in India
🇮🇳 43 of them (nearly 70%) were born here
🍼 9 cubs were born at Kuno National Park in two litters, on 5 October and 20 November
🌿 They now live across 3 sites in Madhya Pradesh: Kuno, Gandhi Sagar and Veerangana Durgavati

Project Cheetah began on 17 September 2022. Thank you to every ranger, vet and villager who keeps watch. 🙏

Save this 🔖 and share it with a wildlife lover.

Sources: PIB via DD India, The Week, Business News Week

posts.headline: A 17-year-old turned a storage room into a *2,000-book library*
posts.sub: In Bengaluru, Asavari Agrawal and student volunteers gave a government school its first library.

slides.title: A school with *only textbooks*
slides.body: The government school in Mullur Colony, Bengaluru, had no library. One of its rooms was used for storage.

slides.title: Nearly five years of showing up
slides.body: Asavari started Shape the Future at 13. Saturdays bring reading hours, sport, art and health camps.

slides.title: From a storage room *to 2,000+ books.* The school's first library.
slides.body: The volunteers turned the storage room into a library stocked with more than 2,000 books.

posts.takeaway: "Start with 10 children, but stay." When young people show up, *futures change.*
posts.source: The Logical Indian (27 Nov 2026), The Better India (13 Nov 2026), Citizen Matters (16 Nov 2026)
posts.caption:
📚 What happens when a teenager never skips a Saturday?

At a government school in Bengaluru's Mullur Colony, children had textbooks but no library. Today, a room once used for storage holds more than 2,000 books.

That change came from 17-year-old Asavari Agrawal and her student volunteers. She started Shape the Future at 13, and for nearly five years they have spent Saturdays on reading hours, sport, art and health camps. About 50 volunteers now reach roughly 250 children. 💛

Her advice to other young people: "Start with 10 children, but stay."

Who kept showing up for you? Tag them below 👇

Sources: The Logical Indian, The Better India, Citizen Matters
